questions.stem: Mitochondrial sheaths are found in which part of the sperm?
questions.solutionHtml:
Middle piece
  • Middle piece: It contains the axial filament in the center that is surrounded by spirally arranged  mitochondrial sheath.


Langman's Medical Embryology, 14th Edition, Page No. 32.

questions.stem: In which stage of meiosis is the primary oocyte arrested?
questions.solutionHtml:
Diplotene
  • Primary oocytes are arrested in the diplotene stage of prophase I of meiosis I.
  • This arrest occurs during fetal development and lasts until a female reaches puberty.


Langman's Medical Embryology, 14th Edition, Page No. 25-26.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the 1st to be formed by the migration of the epiblast along the primitive streak?
questions.solutionHtml:
Endoderm
  • The movement of epiblast cells from the primitive streak and primitive node forms mesoderm and endoderm.
  • The movement of epiblastic mesenchymal cells down the primitive streak is known as ingression.


Langman's Medical Embryology, 14th Edition, Page No. 25-26.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy underwent splenectomy for immune thrombocytopenic purpura. During the procedure, the surgeon noticed bleeding while separating the spleen from the stomach. Which vessel is most likely implicated in this bleeding?
questions.solutionHtml:
Short gastric vessels
  • During a splenectomy, the short gastric vessels and splenic capsule are most commonly injured, resulting in bleeding.


BD Chaurasia’s Human Anatomy, Volume 2, 8th Edition, Page No.295

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a derivative of neural crest cells?
questions.solutionHtml:
Retinal pigment epithelium
  • Retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is derived from the optic neuroepithelium, not neural crest.


Langman's Medical Embryology, 14th Edition, Page No. 95.

questions.stemHtml: The marked structure serves as a surface landmark for which anatomical structure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Stem of lateral sulcus
  • Marked structure is pterion, internally, the pterion is related to various anatomical structures, namely, the anterior division of the middle meningeal vessels, middle cerebral vessels, Sylvain fissure, circle of Willis, insula and Broca's motor speech area (on the left) and optic nerve.



BD Chaurasia’s Human Anatomy, Volume 3, 8th Edition, Page No.29

questions.stem: A 60-year-old male recovering from facial nerve palsy complains of food getting stuck between the cheek and teeth while eating. What is the muscle affected in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Buccinator
  • The food getting stuck between the cheek and teeth while eating, is due to buccinator muscle.


BD Chaurasia’s Human Anatomy, Volume 3, 8th Edition, Page No.87-88
